nina: quick one - onboarding sample (TS + Rollup) breaks when deployed to Edge. local dev + node are fine. anyone seen Rollup + conditional exports weirdness? :thinking:

guillaume: paste the error/logs?

nina: deploy log: `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module` coming from a file under `node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.cjs.js` even though our bundle should be ESM.

sona: that usually means Rollup resolved the package to the CJS entry. do you have an exports map on the SDK package?

nina: published package.json shows only main/module/types and exports only exposes package.json. snippet:
```json
{"main":"dist/index.cjs.js","module":"dist/index.esm.js","types":"dist/index.d.ts","exports":{"./package.json":"./package.json"}}
```

guillaume: yup. Rollup's resolver + plugin-commonjs can rewrite things but SSR/edge builds sometimes pull the cjs file before commonjs conversion, resulting in runtime import syntax errors.

sona: short repro I used: minimal `index.server.ts` with `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'`, `npm i`, then `rollup -c ssr.rollup.js` (with plugin-node-resolve + plugin-commonjs) -> rollup build completes but preview-edge runtime fails with import syntax error.

nina: interestingly, `vite build --ssr` on same code picks the ESM entry and runs fine locally, but preview-edge still failed in our CI preview deploy. inconsistent.

guillaume: two angles: packaging and bundler config. Packaging fix = proper exports map so modern resolvers pick the ESM path by default. e.g. add exports like: { "./": { "import": "./dist/index.esm.js", "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" }, "./package.json": "./package.json" }. That makes resolution deterministic.

sona: bundler-side workarounds for sampleapp onboarding: Rollup: ensure `resolve.mainFields = ['module','main']` (or prefer module in plugin-node-resolve), and run plugin-commonjs after resolve. Example in rollup config: `resolve({ mainFields: ['module','main'] })` and `commonjs({ include: /node_modules/ })`.

nina: we tried `mainFields` but still saw a case where a transitive package lacked exports and Rollup picked the cjs file. aliasing works though: `alias({ entries: [{ find: '@redwood/inference', replacement: path.resolve('node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.esm.js') }] })` — ugly but quick for sampleapp.

guillaume: also watch TS types: if you alias to the ESM file, TypeScript may not pick up `index.d.ts` unless `types` is exported via package `exports` or you add a `types` entry pointing at the d.ts file. So include `types` under exports.

sona: CI suggestion: SDK repo should add a packaging smoke test that publishes a built tarball to a temp dir then runs a small matrix: `rollup -c ssr.rollup.js`, `vite build --ssr`, and `tsc --noEmit` against the sampleapp. Fail the release if any step errors. That would catch both resolution and typing regressions.

ci-bot: created issue sdk-packaging#999: "exports mapping + bundler matrix smoke tests".

pkg-bot: note: CloudEdge runtime enforces ESM semantics for server modules. shipping ESM-first with a CJS fallback is recommended to avoid runtime failures.

nina: helpful. I'll open a PR on the SDK to add an exports map + types entry and include a short repro in the PR description. will also put the alias workaround in the sampleapp README under Onboarding notes.

guillaume: small additional nuance: Rollup plugin order matters. `node-resolve` should run before `commonjs`, and `alias` before both if used. Also ensure `preserveEntrySignatures` is set correctly for SSR builds to avoid renamed exports.

sona: thanks for collecting this. once PR lands ping me and i'll help add the smoke job into SDK CI. this should save a lot of onboarding time. :+1:
